date_note: Version 1.0.7 was released on 24 November according to crypto.news (published 26 November). Crypto Briefing, also 26 November, says Apple reportedly flagged the app that day; the two accounts differ.
exec: A food delivery app that Kaspersky linked to crypto-stealing malware is back on Apple's App Store, crypto.news reports.
plain: Crypto.news reports that Wukong, a food delivery app tied by Kaspersky to the SparkCat crypto-stealing malware in 2025, is back on Apple's App Store under a new publisher. Its release notes do not mention malware removal.

sources.name: Crypto.news: Food delivery app tied to crypto stealing malware returns to App Store
Crypto Briefing: Apple flags Wukong food delivery app as malware for scanning screenshots

summary: Crypto.news reports that Wukong, a food delivery app for Chinese-speaking customers in Thailand, returned to Apple's App Store with version 1.0.7 on 24 November under a new publisher. The article says Kaspersky tied the original app's bundle ID to the SparkCat malware in February 2025 and that Apple reportedly blocked the earlier version in October. It says the release notes do not mention malware removal.
title: Wukong food delivery app, tied by Kaspersky to SparkCat crypto-stealing malware, reportedly returns to App Store

validation.note: Core facts (relaunch, Kaspersky link, release notes) are from crypto.news only. Crypto Briefing says Apple reportedly flagged the app on 26 November, conflicting with crypto.news's October account; it quotes no one. Neither Apple, Kaspersky nor the publisher's own pages were read.
